lower_bound.witness: COUNTEREXAMPLE to the quoted general claim: the sequence of nonnegative integers 3, 2, 1, 0 never increases and starts at a positive value, yet reaches 0. So the stated principle is false. The text has established only that K never increases (two nonunits are replaced by at most two entries) and K=2026 initially; from these premises alone K>=1 at every stage does not follow. The true reason (a legal move needs K>=2 beforehand and lowers K by at most 1, or P'=lcm(m,n)*rest>1) is not written.
lower_bound.load_bearing: The 'exactly one' conclusion of part (a) requires 'at least one nonunit remains', and the text derives this solely from the quoted false principle; the 'at most one' half and termination via lexicographic (P,K) descent are fine.

parsed.notes: Route: (P,K) lexicographic descent for termination; per-prime invariant gcd(v_p) via (a,b)->(min,|a-b|) for choice-independence. Formula for M is correct and its proof is valid. The 'at least one nonunit remains' step rests on a false general statement (nonincreasing positive integer sequence can never reach 0); easily fixable but not fixed in text.
